key_insight: A prompt-engineered large language model can perform QUIPS risk-of-bias assessments for prognosis studies, but its agreement with human reviewers is only modest.
clinical_relevance: If refined and validated, this approach could reduce the time and cost of systematic reviews in neurology and similar fields.
method: Built a zero-shot LLM pipeline to mimic a human reviewer using the QUIPS framework.
Applied the pipeline to 298 articles from 15 published systematic reviews in epilepsy, traumatic brain injury, and stroke.
Compared LLM ratings with original human risk-of-bias assessments and examined inter-rater agreement.
evidence_signal: Across 298 articles, LLM-human agreement was limited (weighted kappa 0.22, 95% CI 0.12-0.33), with statistical differences suggesting humans tended to assign higher risk scores.
watch_item: The comparison against human-human agreement relied on a very small sample (n=5), so performance claims should be interpreted cautiously.
paper_title: A large language model for risk-of-bias assessment in systematic reviews of prognosis studies in clinical neurology
